message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (7 colors × 2 of each number 0‑9 + 2 of each action card + 4 Wild cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches the discard pile’s **color**, **number**, or **symbol**.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile.
• If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, the round ends. That player scores points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points.
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. First to reach the agreed‑upon point total wins the game. | | **Special Rules** | • **Uno Call** – when you have one card left, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes a turn. If you forget, you must draw two cards as a penalty.
• **Stacking** – some house rules allow stacking Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards (e.g., if you’re faced with a Draw Two, you can play another Draw Two to pass the penalty).
• **Card‑Deck Variants** – you can add extra Wild cards or special “Wild Draw Six” cards for more variety. | **Quick Tips** 1. Keep track of the current color and number so you can anticipate opponents’ moves. 2. Use action cards strategically to block opponents or change the direction when you’re close to winning. 3. Remember the “UNO” rule – it’s a simple but crucial part of the game. Enjoy playing Uno!
